subject: Request: HA exhibit & custom orderform language for enterprise onboarding
messages:
From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@novahi.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Black <hannah.black@novahi.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: High-availability exhibit + orderform language

Michael —

Thanks for the call earlier. As we prepare for legal review, procurement asked me to send a short note outlining the exact availability guarantees we need to see in an exhibit attached to the MSA + the specific orderform wording for the Dedicated capacity purchase. Our requirements are: 1) a 99.95% monthly uptime commitment for production GPUs, 2) latency SLOs for p95 inference latency under typical batch sizes, and 3) an agreed evidence package for outages (root cause summary, time to remediation, and telemetry extracts).

Can you provide a proposed HA exhibit and a draft of the orderform language that maps to the pricing tier we discussed? Attached is a high-level procurement checklist (NovaHi_SLA_Addendum_Request.pdf). We'd like to have an initial draft to legal by EOD Thursday.

Appreciate it —
Jake
Procurement Manager
NovaHi Health

Attachments: NovaHi_SLA_Addendum_Request.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@novahi.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High-availability exhibit + orderform language

Hi Jake —

Thanks for the checklist and for laying out the asks clearly. I've attached a first-pass HA exhibit and an orderform draft scoped to the Dedicated capacity configuration we discussed (redwood_ha_exhibit_v1.docx, OrderForm_NovaHi_20270620_draft.docx). Key callouts up front:

- We can commit to 99.95% monthly availability for production instances in the committed Dedicated pool, with credits defined in the exhibit tied to measured downtime windows (not including scheduled maintenance windows with prior notice).
- Latency SLOs: we propose p95 inference latency targets per model-class (small/medium/large) and a clause that allows for temporary degradation with automated fallback to a compatible model variant to preserve request success.
- Evidence package: we include a remediation summary template, pre-formatted telemetry exports, and a 30-day incident postmortem timeline.

A couple of open items I'd like your team to confirm: the definition of "scheduled maintenance" you'd accept (e.g., up to 4 hours/month for major kernel upgrades vs. 30 minutes/month for minor patches) and whether NovaHi needs telemetry extracts beyond aggregated downtime windows (we can provide token-level traces under NDA but need to confirm scope).

If this looks directionally correct, I'll loop Legal to produce a redline-friendly PDF and ask Monica to surface any internal impact to SLA bonuses/credits.

Best,
Michael Grant
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_ha_exhibit_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), OrderForm_NovaHi_20270620_draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High-availability exhibit + orderform language

Michael —

Quick internal read from Procurement/Legal ops: the exhibit is a good start, but Legal will want clearer language on evidence deliverables and the timing for credits. Also: the SLA credits table currently references "hourly service disruption" which Legal prefers to map to incident windows (start/end timestamps) and total impacted requests rather than a simple hourly bucket.

Notes for Aditya (tech): can we confirm that providing token-level traces for customers under NDA is feasible for Dedicated customers? If not, propose a sanitized telemetry export we can guarantee within 48 hours of a request.

Laura — can you check the orderform draft and confirm that the price banding lines up with the committed vGPU counts? We need to ensure procurement can tie the availability exhibit to the specific orderform SKU.

Thanks —
Monica
Enterprise Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High-availability exhibit + orderform language

Monica / Michael —

Short tech confirmation: for Dedicated customers in the committed pool we can provide: 1) incident start/end timestamps and per-cluster request success rates as standard exports, 2) aggregated token/latency histograms for the affected time windows, and 3) limited raw trace extracts under NDA for specific investigations (we'll need a legal data request form). The team estimates a 24–72 hour turnaround for the exported telemetry depending on sample size.

Regarding scheduled maintenance: our standard for major maintenance is to notify customers at least 72 hours in advance for anything >1 hour. We can accept carve-outs for emergency maintenance but would log those separately and treat them as non-creditable unless caused by Redwood.

Happy to join a quick call with NovaHi legal to walk through what telemetry looks like.

—Aditya
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Black <hannah.black@novahi.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Jake Turner <jake.turner@novahi.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: High-availability exhibit + orderform language

Michael / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the detailed exhibit. Legal reviewed redwood_ha_exhibit_v1 and provided inline comments; the main asks are: 1) clarity on the credit calculation (percent of monthly fees vs. fixed per-incident credit), 2) inclusion of a commit to provide a post-incident RCA within 10 business days for Sev 1 incidents, and 3) an explicit statement that backups of NovaHi data used for inference will not be used for model training.

We attached a short comment summary and a suggested credit table (see attached: NovaHi_SLA_Addendum_Request.pdf — updated). If you can confirm the RCA timeline and non-training clause, we can move forward with a redline exchange and target execution next week. Also happy to set a 30-minute legal-to-legal call — Wednesday morning PT works for us.

Regards,
Hannah Black
Head of Legal Operations
NovaHi Health

Attachments: NovaHi_SLA_Addendum_Request.pdf (updated comments, application/pdf)
